children.topic: Gross Anatomy & Relations
Retroperitoneal organ (except tail which lies in splenorenal ligament)
Anatomical Regions: Head (embraced by C-loop of duodenum), Uncinate Process (posterior to SMA/SMV), Neck (anterior to SMA/SMV union), Body, Tail (touches splenic hilum)
Posterior Relations: IVC, Aorta, SMA, Left renal vein, Splenic vein, Common Bile Duct (grooves posterior head)
Ductal System
Main Pancreatic Duct (Wirsung): Drains tail, body, posterior head → joins CBD at Ampulla of Vater → opens at Major Duodenal Papilla
Accessory Duct (Santorini): Drains anterior head → opens 2 cm proximal at Minor Duodenal Papilla
Pancreas Divisum (Most common congenital anomaly - 5-10%): Failure of dorsal & ventral ducts to fuse → main drainage via small accessory duct → risk of recurrent pancreatitis
Annular Pancreas: Ring of pancreatic tissue encircling D2 of duodenum → neonatal duodenal obstruction (Double bubble sign on X-ray)
Vascular Supply & Drainage
Head & Uncinate Process: Superior Pancreaticoduodenal A. (from GDA) & Inferior Pancreaticoduodenal A. (from SMA) → Celiac-SMA collateral bed
Body & Tail: Splenic Artery (branches: Dorsal pancreatic, Great pancreatic, Caudal pancreatic arteries)
Venous Drainage: Portal system via Splenic vein and SMV
Lymphatics: Drains to pancreaticosplenic, celiac, and superior mesenteric lymph nodes
Exocrine & Endocrine Physiology
Exocrine (85% mass): Acinar cells produce Zymogens (Trypsinogen, Chymotrypsinogen, Lipase, Amylase); Duct cells secrete HCO₃⁻ (neutralizes gastric acid via Secretin stimulation)
Endocrine (Islets of Langerhans - 1-2% mass):
Alpha (α) cells (20%): Glucagon
Beta (β) cells (70%): Insulin, C-peptide, Amylin
Delta (δ) cells (5%): Somatostatin
PP (F) cells: Pancreatic polypeptide
